(a) Ibn Ezra does not object that Isaac died when Joseph was 29: he says the ancients applied 'his father wept' to Isaac and that in truth Isaac did not die until Joseph was 29, i.e. he was still alive. Rewrite so Ibn Ezra reports the midrash and confirms Isaac was alive (Radak computes the same); the plain sense is still Jacob. (b) Drop the claim that Ibn Ezra faults Onkelos for making sheolah Gehenna: Onkelos in the packet reads 'to Sheol' and Pseudo-Jonathan 'to the house of burial'. Say only that Ibn Ezra takes sheolah as 'the grave' and criticises an unnamed translator. Fix the philological notes on sheolah and 'his father' the same way.

Considered a causal link from the coat of many colours (evt.gen_37.joseph_reports_and_coat) to the conspiracy. Dropped because the cause is stated only as hatred, which is inside one event; the dreams are named by the brothers (v19-20).

The packet's reviewer requests (ENABLES instead of TRIGGERS; DAY_SEQUENCE and REGNAL_YEAR tiers; a shorter jacob_mourns; extra causal links) address the chronologist's work. I did not change any event, timing or causal link here: they need a /urim-chronologist GEN.37 revision. Event ids stay the same, so these participants and states still fit.

[event:evt.gen_37.jacob_mourns] Revised on request: the event is the mourning itself (weeks to months), not 22 years. Rashi's 22 years run to the descent into Egypt, already dated by the Joseph anchor. Later chapters can anchor on this event's END only as 'some weeks or months after the coat', not as the end of the grief.

[event:evt.gen_37.sheaf_dream] The two dreams (v5-8, v9-11) are likely to be fulfilled in GEN.42-47 (brothers bow to Joseph, 42:6; 43:26; 44:14; Jacob 46-47). Those chapters' sessions should write FULFILLS_PROPHECY from these events. I did not write them here as the effect events are not in the corpus. There is no divine speech in this chapter, so no link in it is FULFILLS_PROPHECY. The dream of the moon/mother: Rachel is dead (Gen 35:19); not a dating matter.

[causal:caus.gen_37.joseph_reports_and_coat.brothers_conspire] Added on request as ENABLES: the hatred of v4 is the standing motive; the dreams (v8, 19-20) are the explicit one.

[verse.en:GEN.37.15] The stranger is left unnamed in both layers. Rashi and Pseudo-Jonathan make him Gabriel, Ramban reports the Midrash that these men are angels; Ibn Ezra says a passerby. Kept as commentary only.

[verse.en:GEN.37.18] The suggestion that the long tunic made Joseph recognisable from afar is my own and is flagged as such in the commentary. Ramban's claim that they first tried a trick and failed is his conjecture ('perhaps').

[verse.en:GEN.37.19] Ba'al as the Canaanite god's name is background knowledge, unsourced. The five English versions all say 'dreamer'; I chose 'master of the dreams' for the literal layer because ba'al plus the article is a title.
[verse.en:GEN.37.20] That Jacob's own words at v. 33 repeat chayyah ra'ah akhalatehu is from my reading of v. 33, not from the packet. The remark on cisterns is general background.
[verse.en:GEN.37.21] The reference to Exodus 33:11 is Ibn Ezra's, carried over from the packet. The Bilhah episode is Sforno's association of Reuben's rescue with 35:22 and 49:4.

[verse.en:GEN.37.23] STEPBible glosses hapasim as 'the palms and soles'; glossed here as 'the pasim' (see GEN.37.3). The nakedness reading is Ibn Ezra's, not the text's, and is marked so in the commentary.

[verse.en:GEN.37.24] The statement that cisterns run low at the end of the dry summer is general background and unsourced. 'Simeon' for the taker is Radak quoting Genesis Rabbah. The link to bor in 40:15 is my own observation.

[verse.en:GEN.37.25] Identity of nekhot and lot is disputed; the packet's glosses (spice, myrrh) are kept only as the KJV tradition, and I gloss them 'spice-gum' and 'ladanum' with the Hebrew words in the literal layer. The Abraham 22:13 parallel and the yarad echo are my own observations.

[verse.en:GEN.37.27] The Exodus 21:16 point and the 20-shekel price (Lev 27:5) are my own knowledge; they come from no commentary in the packet. The claim that the later law's penalty applies is an irony for the reader, not a legal argument.

[verse.en:GEN.37.28] Ambiguous subject (see the ontology note on joseph_sold). The literal and dramatic layers keep the Hebrew's unmarked plural verbs; the commentary lists Rashbam, Rashi, Radak/Ibn Ezra and Ramban. The weight of 20 shekels (about 230 g) assumes a shekel of about 11.4 g, which is my figure.
[verse.en:GEN.37.29] Rashi's and Radak's accounts of where Reuben was are rabbinic reconstruction; the text gives none.
[verse.en:GEN.37.31] The 'kid' versus 'he-goat' point is mine: se'ir is a male goat, gedi a kid. The goat-skin irony with Gen 27 is my own observation.

[verse.en:GEN.37.32] The Tamar parallel (38:25) is Radak's, citing Genesis Rabbah; the link to 42:8 is my own. The 'tore it with a blade' reading of vayshalechu is reported from Ramban, Radak and Sforno.
[verse.en:GEN.37.33] The Potiphar's-wife reading of chayyah ra'ah is Rashi's, from the Midrash; Pseudo-Jonathan has a different gloss (an evil woman). Ibn Ezra's grammatical comment is summarised.

[verse.en:GEN.37.36] The packet's token 1 carries a marker (L(E)); I read the word as Medanites, the Masoretic form, and did not harmonise it with v. 28 in the literal layer. Potiphar's name etymology is my own background knowledge. The KJV is said to 'harmonise' on the strength of its rendering Midianites in both verses.
